matches.title: An elementary counterexample to Long's clique equality
matches.description:
The full ring of integers of Q(sqrt(10)) gives a complete elementary negative answer to the equality printed in Long Question 7.2 (arXiv:1512.04620v1), using its prime-element convention and without a PID assumption. Both the unit-difference and unit-or-prime-element-difference graphs have clique number two, and the least norm of a nonzero prime ideal is two. The displayed proposed equality therefore compares two with four.

This is a credited elementary exposition, with no claim of novelty, firstness, current worldwide openness, or independent discovery lineage. Lenstra's 1977 Proposition 2.2 already supplies the ideal-residue unit-clique bound. Dummit's 2021 notes explicitly contain the same classical ideal and norm obstruction. Long and Thistlethwaite supply the prime-clique framework; Lopez's 2018 thesis defines the same first prime graph and related higher prime-ideal-power graphs. Combining old ingredients here is not backdated as an earlier printed resolution. The exact historical priority of the full graph conclusion remains unestablished after the scoped audit.

The prime-element convention means a nonzero nonunit generating a prime ideal. It does not mean irreducible element and does not impose the additional Lenstra-Hurwitz unit-surjectivity condition. Higher prime-ideal-power graphs are different for powers at least two. The note computes the quantities in the printed question directly, independently of the journal theorem whose displayed minimum is over principal ideals.

The supporting archive retains the manuscript, immutable original submission, explicit current adjudications, authored mathematical and priority reviews, source-read receipts, and scoped reproducible finite checks. Omitted third-party bodies and the original raw search excerpt ledger are not claimed as portable members. AI tools were used extensively in solving, reconstruction, source review, verification, drafting, and independent internal AI adversarial review. This work is unrefereed; no external human peer review, formal proof-assistant certification, or journal acceptance is claimed. Finite checks are diagnostics rather than a substitute for the written proof.

matches.title: A credited finiteness deduction for restricted boundary-twist factorizations
matches.description: For each fixed genus g ≥ 1, let S(g,1) be an oriented compact surface with one boundary component, and let maps and isotopies fix that boundary pointwise. We prove that ordered positive factorizations of one positive boundary Dehn twist, along non-null-homotopic simple closed curves with repetitions permitted and pairwise geometric intersection at most one, have finitely many simultaneous-conjugacy classes. Their maximal length M(g) is finite and attained, with M(g) ≥ 4g(2g+1). Peripheral factors occur only in the singleton factorization; otherwise all factors are nonseparating. The values M(1) = 12 and M(2) = 40 are credited deductions from prior work with the convention bridge stated. This gives a complete negative answer, under the stated conventions, to the separately printed restricted arbitrary-length clause in the Wajnryb/Farb problem collection. The full original maximum and classification bundle remains partial: exact M(g) for g ≥ 3, explicit upper formulas, an effective exhaustive-enumeration stopping criterion, extremizers, and Hurwitz, positive Artin, T-move and A5/D6 classifications remain unresolved in this work. The note is a credited deduction and exposition. Cossu and Tringali's arXiv:2208.05869v3, Corollary 4.13, supplies the generic finite-alphabet finiteness corollary through a normal reduced cone and nonerasing atomic expansions. The support and ribbon arguments explicitly build on Juvan–Malnič–Mohar, Malestein–Rivin–Theran, and Cahn–Fanoni–Petri. Honda–Kazez–Matić, Smith, the chain relation, and Baykur–Monden–Van Horn-Morris provide credited premises. Exact historical priority of the resulting surface application, novelty, and worldwide current-open status remain UNKNOWN; a bounded literature audit is not an absence proof. Extensive AI tools were used in mathematical and source checking, writing, code, and package preparation. This preprint is unrefereed, has no external human peer review, and is not formally certified. The accompanying verification kit provides written proof and source/custody records plus reproducible finite fault controls; those controls do not replace the universal proof or replay omitted historical inputs.

matches.title: Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient
matches.description: We classify positive words in the five fixed standard generators of B6 modulo c=h representing c^2. The possible lengths are 20, 30 and 40, with respectively one, one and two strict Hurwitz classes. Simultaneous conjugation identifies the two length-40 classes, giving the three proposed representatives of Wajnryb's quotient question. A pure-braid linking reduction and an exhaustive exact 810-word certificate settle length 20. The classical group presentation, previously known length spectrum and Casson's twice-per-pair crossing assertion reported by Elrifai-Morton are explicitly credited. A full reproducible six-strand crossing certificate and independent controls accompany the note. Novelty of the exact complete classification is not certified by a negative literature search. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, literature research, writing and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint and has not received external human peer review. The statement is restricted to fixed-generator input words, not arbitrary conjugate-factor or geometric factorizations.

matches.title: Exact Diffusion Design for Maximally Collective Stable Turing Patterns in Binary-Complex Mass-Action Networks
matches.description:
For every n ≥ 4, this preprint constructs an n-species binary-complex classical mass-action topology for which, throughout every positive-equilibrium realization, every principal subsystem below order n − 1 is Hurwitz while one order-(n − 1) subsystem is unstable. A general principal-minor diffusion-ray theorem yields an exact network law: for any homogeneously stable realization, a stationary crossing occurs along a positive diagonal diffusion ray exactly when d_Z > 8 h_Z Σ_{j=2}^{n−2} d_j/h_j. This gives the nonattained fixed-equilibrium contrast infimum, the unit-equilibrium value 8(n − 3), and the topology-wide stationary trade-off χ_D χ_H > 8(n − 3).

At unit equilibrium, an exact rational design undergoes a primary supercritical bifurcation with locally exponentially stable positive patterns in the fixed-integrated-mass class. A second exact family redistributes heterogeneity between diffusion and equilibrium concentrations so that both contrasts are Θ(√n), matching the topology-specific stationary minimax lower bound in exponent. The proof uses explicit flux-cone design, exhaustive strongly connected block classification, conservation-compatible center-manifold reduction, and inspectable symbolic certificates.

The networks are synthetic. The bifurcation, stability, and robustness conclusions are local for each fixed dimension, and the stationary diffusion law does not classify arbitrary wave instability. This is a submission-ready author preprint and has not undergone journal peer review.

Version 1.0.11 includes the main preprint, mathematical supplement, self-contained TeX source, portable exact-verification repository, and a separate data archive. The exact companion software release is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22625980.
